creator: Anonymous
model: NIMFA SIS dynamics dx_i/dt = -delta_i x_i + (1 - x_i)(Bx)_i on [0,1]^n with nonnegative (possibly time-varying or directed) infection matrix B; y(t) is the average infection level; R0 = rho(B) for unit recovery.

definitions.h: h(s) = -s - log(1 - s), the Volterra-type function
definitions.kappa(G): critical constant (5.2) of the leading eigenvector, limit of t y(t) at the threshold
definitions.T(r): upper-transition time of Persoons et al. (their eq. 8)

claims.statement: Spectral Riccati envelope: under a quadratic-form condition (D), a weighted average of h(x_i) = -x_i - log(1 - x_i) obeys a scalar Riccati comparison, and Jensen's inequality transfers it to the weighted average of x_i. (D) holds for symmetric infection matrices, time-varying networks, node-dependent recovery and, with Perron weights, directed networks.
claims.scope: NIMFA-type systems (2.1) with piecewise continuous data.
claims.evidence: written proof in nimfa_envelopes.pdf; symbolic and numerical checks in VERIFICATION.md

claims.statement: Conjecture 1 of Persoons et al. (2024): for symmetric B >= 0 with spectral radius at most 1 and unit recovery, y(t) <= 1/(1+t) for every initial state and t >= 0 (more precisely, the Riccati envelope with rate 1 - rho).
claims.scope: Graph may be disconnected; time in mean recovery times.
claims.evidence: written proof in nimfa_envelopes.pdf; symbolic and numerical checks in VERIFICATION.md

claims.statement: Conjecture 2, sharpened: above threshold on a connected graph, starting at or above the endemic equilibrium p, the excess y(t) - y_inf is at most (1 - p_bar)/(1+t), with an exponential form.
claims.scope: Symmetric irreducible B, unit recovery, p <= x(0) <= u.
claims.evidence: written proof in nimfa_envelopes.pdf; symbolic and numerical checks in VERIFICATION.md

claims.statement: The envelope is attained by regular graphs (so the constant 1 cannot be lowered), and the subcritical exponent 1 - rho is exact for every connected graph.
claims.evidence: written proof in nimfa_envelopes.pdf; symbolic and numerical checks in VERIFICATION.md

claims.statement: At the threshold, t x_i(t) converges for every node and nonzero initial state to v_i / sum_j u_j delta_j v_j^2 (directed and heterogeneous recovery included); for the population average the limit is kappa(G) <= 1, with equality iff the graph is regular; the transition time satisfies r T(r) -> kappa(G).
claims.scope: The 1/t mechanism is the standard centre-manifold reduction; the global statement, constants and characterisation are the proposed contribution.
claims.evidence: written proof in nimfa_envelopes.pdf; symbolic and numerical checks in VERIFICATION.md

claims.statement: Node-wise: x_i(t) <= sqrt(n/(t(1+t))) at or below threshold, and the worst asymptotic node constant has order exactly n^(1/3).
claims.scope: Symmetric B, unit recovery; the uniform-in-time order is open.
claims.evidence: written proof in nimfa_envelopes.pdf; symbolic and numerical checks in VERIFICATION.md

claims.statement: Stronger statements fail: the unweighted average can break the bound on directed networks (explicit two-node example), and the arithmetic-mean parameter does not suffice.
claims.evidence: written proof in nimfa_envelopes.pdf; symbolic and numerical checks in VERIFICATION.md

claims.statement: The envelopes hold for the infectious fraction in SIR/SIRS network models and for the expected prevalence of the exact Markovian SIS process with a common recovery rate (via Simon and Kiss 2018).
claims.scope: Stochastic statement is an upper bound only; common recovery rate; independent initial states.
claims.evidence: written proof in nimfa_envelopes.pdf; symbolic and numerical checks in VERIFICATION.md

claims.statement: Mixed initial states never converge slower than both extremes; unconditional transition-time bounds hold for all R0, exact for regular graphs and conservative on strongly heterogeneous ones.
claims.scope: Answers the timescale-separation question of Persoons et al. under the stated hypotheses.
claims.evidence: written proof in nimfa_envelopes.pdf; symbolic and numerical checks in VERIFICATION.md

claims.statement: On synthetic networks of 1000 nodes kappa ranges from about 0.92 (Watts-Strogatz) to about 0.035 (random geometric); at R0 = 1 the time for the average to fall below 0.1% is about 922 versus 39 recovery times. Two solvers show the growth formula of Persoons et al. (eq. 20) under-estimates the growth time within its hypotheses away from R0 -> 1.
claims.scope: Numerical, fixed seeds, synthetic networks; eq. (20) failures not interval-certified.
